question: Which Chola ruler is credited with the construction of irrigation systems to support agriculture?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajendra Chola I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rajendra Chola I, the son of Raja Raja Chola I, ruled the Chola dynasty from 1014 to 1044 CE and expanded its territory significantly.
 
• He is credited with constructing advanced irrigation systems, including tanks, reservoirs, and canals, to boost agricultural productivity in the Chola Empire.
 
• The Chola rulers, under Rajendra Chola I, focused on water management and utilized river systems like the Kaveri to create sustainable agricultural practices.
 
• Rajendra Chola I established the city of Gangaikonda Cholapuram and built extensive infrastructure to support his empire’s agrarian economy.
 
• His irrigation initiatives were pivotal in transforming the fertile lands of the Tamil region into one of the most prosperous agricultural zones during his reign.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chola Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Chola dynasty was one of the longest-ruling dynasties in Indian history, with its origins tracing back to the 9th century CE.
 
• They were renowned for their contributions to art, architecture, administration, and infrastructure development.
 
• The Cholas built iconic temples such as the Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 
 
• **Irrigation Systems:**
 
 
• Ancient Indian rulers prioritized irrigation systems to ensure sustainable agricultural practices and food security.
 
• Techniques included the use of canals, tanks, and reservoirs for water storage and distribution.
 
• The Kaveri delta region was a crucial area for irrigation development during the Chola period.
 
 
 
• **Gangaikonda Cholapuram:**
 
 
• Rajendra Chola I established Gangaikonda Cholapuram as the capital of the Chola Empire.
 
• The city featured advanced urban planning and infrastructure, including temples and irrigation systems.
 
• It served as a symbol of Chola power and prosperity during his reign.
 
 
 
• **Agrarian Economy:**
 
 
• The Chola dynasty depended heavily on agriculture for economic stability and expansion.
 
• Efficient irrigation systems allowed the cultivation of crops like rice, which was a staple food for the population.
 
• The agrarian economy fueled trade and commerce, making the Chola Empire a prominent player in regional and international trade.
